task1.question: Is there a locus-reading rule, computed only from the engine's own outputs (boundary support landscape, significant pairs, modules), that draws tighter boundaries without losing loci?
task1.arm: rescue3 = engine/results_dpann_repair/dpann__mmseqs__seq__e3c50s75_rescue3__w3 (current DPANN default, w3, rule P<=1e-4&L>=2)

landscape_definitions.b: boundary_support.npy: max genera L over significant instances spanning the boundary (reproduced exactly from tokens + significant_pairs.parquet)
landscape_definitions.arg: significant pair that sets b (engine tie rule)
landscape_definitions.bJ: max J over significant instances spanning the boundary
landscape_definitions.pair module: Louvain module shared by both tokens of the pair (-1 between modules); Louvain on the significant-pair token graph, weight J*log2(max(L,2)), seed 17, as the engine
landscape_definitions.level-2 locus: maximal run of boundaries with b >= 2 (conserved@2, the default reading)

A_trim.definition: (a) relative trimming: drop end genes of each level-2 locus while the end boundary's b < f * median b of the untrimmed locus

B_level.definition: (b) per-locus level: for each level-2 locus, among ladder levels (2,3,5,8,12,20,30,50,80,120,200,300,500,800) <= its max b, read the runs at the level maximizing the mean edge contrast log(mean b of the h boundaries inside an edge) - log(max(mean b of the h boundaries outside, 1)) (outside stops at the level-2 locus end); a level above 2 needs contrast >= level-2 contrast + gain; keep_low=0 reports only the runs at the chosen level, keep_low=1 also reports the stretches between them (>= 2 genes; the junction gene stays with the run), i.e. a segmentation

C_module.definition: (c) module-consistent segmentation: inside each level-2 locus, boundary labels = module of the pair that sets b (-1/-2 filled from the nearest labelled boundary, forward then backward); cut where the label changes; the shared junction gene stays with the side whose junction boundary has the larger b

D_nested.definition: (d) nested output: the level-2 locus (neighbourhood) plus a core inside it; scored as the two-reading table (best locus per instance; ribosomal best = largest overlap, ties to the shorter locus, as ribosomal_check.py). The core alone is the corresponding single rule.

grid.core: every config of A_trim, B_level with keep_low=0, F_fixed, C_module and E_consistency

E_consistency.definition: added rule: runs of boundaries with bJ >= theta (a boundary is kept only if a significant pair spanning it co-locates consistently relative to its rarer token)

task1.scoring: score_dpann_loci.score, min_members 2, 200 controls, seed 17; ribosomal: ribosomal_check.score/summarize on g2 runs with >= 16 marked genes (1,686; 848 odd, 838 even), resolved = best locus covers >= 80% at precision >= 0.8, recovered = best covers >= 50%.

references.R2_secondary: the engine's full locus table loci_all_genomes.parquet (11 readings, best per instance), the source of every DPANN F1 in the notebook

tuning.data: odd genome_code only: odd-genome gold instances (shadow package pkg_odd) and the 848 odd-genome ribosomal runs
tuning.per_family_selection: lexicographic: (1) number of the three adoption conditions met on odd genomes against R1, with the ribosomal thresholds scaled to the odd runs (resolved >= 554 of 848, recovered >= 830 of 848, Parvarchaeaceae >= 54 of 55; ceil of the scaled 1,100 / 1,650 / 110), condition (ii) as point estimate summed DF+TXSS excess - R1 >= +0.02, condition (iii) each caller F1 - R1 >= -0.01; (2) larger odd summed DF+TXSS excess
tuning.families: B_level counts as one family (keep_low is a parameter); D_nested is one family over all cores

adoption_criteria_test.data: even genome_code gold instances; ribosomal on all 1,686 runs as the condition states (even-run subset also reported)
adoption_criteria_test.i: ribosomal resolved >= 1,100 of 1,686 AND recovered >= 1,650 AND Parvarchaeaceae recovered >= 110 of 114
adoption_criteria_test.ii: summed DefenseFinder + TXSScan excess (rule - R1) >= +0.02 AND its 95% paired genome-bootstrap interval excludes 0 (2,000 draws, seed 17, genomes resampled jointly for both callers, as dpann_compare.py)
adoption_criteria_test.iii: no caller (DefenseFinder, TXSScan, CRISPRCasTyper) loses more than 0.01 F1 against R1 (point estimate; interval reported)
adoption_criteria_test.adopt: all three. If several families pass, the preferred one has the larger odd summed excess. Every family's selected config is reported against all three conditions, with the blocking condition named.
adoption_criteria_test.secondary: the same three conditions against R2 for the same selected configs (no re-tuning); reported as whether the rule could replace the engine's full table

refutation.tighter_without_losing_loci: refuted for a rule if its median boundary precision rises while covered50 falls by > 0.01 for any caller or ribosomal recovered falls below 1,650 (tighter by dropping loci), or if its excess gain comes with an F1 loss (control falling faster than F1)
refutation.rule_vs_families: the rule does the work if its gain over each arm's own R1 has the same sign and comparable size (within a factor of 2) on the base (no rescue) and hybrid arms; the families do the work if the gain appears on one arm only

task1.follow_up_arms: the adopted rule (or, if none passes, the two families with the most conditions met on even, then larger even summed excess; descriptive only) with its rescue3-tuned parameters, unchanged, on base = engine/results_dpann_v5/dpann__mmseqs__seq__e3c50s75__w3 and hybrid = engine/results_dpann_emb1/dpann__hybrid__esmpp_small__genomecentred__e3c50cpmr0p05__w3, each against its own R1 and R2 on even genomes plus the ribosomal check

task2.question: Does treating each adjacent broken-call-like split pair (38,651 pairs, repair/results/split_pairs.parquet) as one gene position raise localization of the gold instances that contain such a pair, without lowering the rest?
task2.build: merge_universe.py: every gb (= ga + 1) merges into the position of gb - 1 (chains collapse to one position); merged gene keeps the first piece's identifiers, start = min, end = max; positions, gids, contig n_genes / first_gid and genome n_genes recomputed; gold member gids mapped and deduplicated; the merged position takes the rescue3 token of its longest piece (ties: lowest old gid). Package untouched; everything under $RD/boundary/merged/.
task2.engine: unmodified $RD/engine/code/recurrence.py on the merged universe, rescue3 tokens as above, w 3, genome-shuffle null, 3 permutations, rule chosen by the engine (FDR <= 0.01, largest coverage), --all-genome-loci; scored with score_dpann_loci.py --min-members 2 on the merged package (full locus table, as the engine wrapper).

sets.contains_pair: both pieces of a split pair among the instance's members and >= 2 members after merging
sets.unaffected: no piece of any split pair inside the instance's first-to-last member span (>= 2 members in both universes)
sets.touched: any member is a piece, >= 2 members after merging
sets.left: instances whose members merge into one position (leave the >= 2-member set); counted by caller

criteria_even_genomes.a: mean F1 on contains_pair instances, merged - default >= +0.03, 95% paired genome-bootstrap interval excluding 0 (2,000 draws, seed 17)
criteria_even_genomes.b: summed DefenseFinder + TXSScan excess on unaffected instances, merged - default, 95% lower bound > -0.005

task2.also_reported: the same on remaining and touched sets, per caller, odd genomes; engine significant pairs, FDR, genes covered; ribosomal check in the merged universe (runs remapped); the task-1 adopted rule D (level-2 + level-200 core) read on both universes and compared the same way
task2.caveat: merging changes the genome-shuffle null (fewer genes per genome) and the random-placement control (spans in genes change), so merged and unmerged excess differ in both terms
task2.refutation: if F1 on contains_pair instances rises only through instances whose span shrinks to fewer genes while the control rises equally (excess flat), the gain is a coordinate effect of merging, not localization; reported via the excess on the same set
